item.title: New faces named in Fijian 7s and Fijiana squads for Dubai and Cape Town
item.description: Several new faces will feature in the Fiji Airways Men's and Fijiana National 7s teams for the opening two legs of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town. The men's team will feature debutants Vilimone Raiqiso, Aquino Savenaca, Sanaila Daliga and Saimone Qeleca.
item.content:encoded:
Several new faces will feature in the Fiji Airways Men's and Fijiana National 7s teams for the opening two legs of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town.

The men's team will feature debutants Vilimone Raiqiso, Aquino Savenaca, Sanaila Daliga and Saimone Qeleca.

Tira Wilagi has been named captain of the side, with Akuila Dranivotua, Joseva Talacolo, Kavekini Tanivanuakula, George Bose and Aquino Savenaca also included in the starting line-up.

The reserves are Douglas Daveta, Iowane Teba, Ratu Filipe Sauturaga, Sanaila Daliga, Vuiviwa Naduvalo and Saimone Qeleca.

Meanwhile, the Fijiana 7s team will feature debutants Merewarita Neivosa, Kelerayani Luvu and Regan Chapman.

Ana Naimasi has been named captain of the Fijiana side, with Sesenieli Donu, Adi Salote Nailolo, Laisani Moceisawana, Reapi Ulunisau, Varanisese Qoro and Kelerayani Luvu named in the starting line-up.

The reserves are Mariana Talatoka, Regan Chapman, Atelaite Ralivanawana, Ivi Savu and Mere Vocevoce.

The Fiji Men's 7s team will face defending champions New Zealand in their opening pool match next Saturday at 8.36pm, before taking on France at 11.17pm.

They will face Spain in their final pool match on Sunday at 4am.

Meanwhile, the Fijiana 7s team will face Canada in their opening pool match next Saturday at 6.44pm, followed by Japan at 9.44pm.

They will take on New Zealand in their final pool match on Sunday at 2.52am.

item.title: Brown to lead Police in bid for fifth consecutive Ratu Sukuna Bowl title
item.description: Former Fiji Airways national 7s player James Brown will lead Police today as they aim to defend the Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl trophy against Army. Brown has been part of the Police team's four consecutive title wins and will bring his experience and leadership as the men from Nasova aim to make it five in a row.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji Airways national 7s player James Brown will lead Police today as they aim to defend the Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl trophy against Army.

Brown has been part of the Police team's four consecutive title wins and will bring his experience and leadership as the men from Nasova aim to make it five in a row.

The Nadi rugby player will look to use his experience to control play in today's clash.

The Police front row consists of Timoci Sauvoli, Rusiate Navuma (VC) and Jone Naqiri.

Brown, Jolame Levevou, Sakiusa Vosayaco, Saimoni Seruvatu and Vunaki Waqanibau have also been named in the forwards.

Sefanaia Seviua will start at scrum-half, while Etonia Rokotuisawa will play at fly-half.

Jone Dukumoi, Waisake Ravuiwasa, Jack Volavola, Rusiate Matai and Ponipate Tuberi complete the backline.

Meanwhile, Army's front row consists of Simione Bulai, Patemo Nuku and Joseva Nasaroa.

Nadidi Taginaselala will captain Army from the second row, where he will partner Sitiveni Kurivitu.

Ebenezer Tuidraki, Avisa Anaqali and Saimone Wakanivesi have also been named in the forwards.

Joji Vusoniyasi will start at halfback, pairing with Anare Tabakaucoro at fly-half.

Jope Raderua, Solomoni Naiduku, Joji Wainiqolo, Peni Rokoduguni and Ilikena Vudogo complete the backline.

Police will face Army at 4pm today at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

item.title: Jake White makes changes as Marika Parker eyes Flying Fijians debut against Italy
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians coach Jake White has made a few changes to his line-up for Sunday's Nations Championship clash against Italy, with 24-year-old tighthead prop Marika Parker in line to make his debut off the bench. White has retained the same front row of Peni Ravai, captain Tevita Ikanivere and Luke Tagi.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians coach Jake White has made a few changes to his line-up for Sunday's Nations Championship clash against Italy, with 24-year-old tighthead prop Marika Parker in line to make his debut off the bench.

White has retained the same front row of Peni Ravai, captain Tevita Ikanivere and Luke Tagi.

Setareki Tuiragacoke and Isoa Nasilasila are the locks.

Mesake Vocevoce and Kitione Salawa are the flankers, with Nathan Hughes returning at No. 8.

Frank Lomani starts at halfback, with Ben Volavola at flyhalf.

Josua Tuisova and Setareki Bituniyata form the midfield combination.

Jiuta Wainiqolo starts on the left wing, Selestino Ravutaumada on the right wing, with Ponipate Loganimasi at fullback.

The replacements are Zuriel Togiatama, Vilikesa Nairau, Marika Parker, Joseva Tamani, Etonia Waqa, Terio Tamani, Caleb Muntz and Iosefo Masi.

The Flying Fijians take on Italy at 4.40am on Sunday.

item.title: Army thump Police 38-14 in Sukuna Bowl Rugby League clash
item.description: The Republic of Fiji Military Forces Rugby League team thumped Police 38-14 this afternoon at Buckhurst Park in Suva. Army had a commanding 20-8 lead at half-time.
item.content:encoded:
The Republic of Fiji Military Forces Rugby League team thumped Police 38-14 this afternoon at Buckhurst Park in Suva.

Army had a commanding 20-8 lead at half-time.

In other sports, Police beat Army 50-44 in Women's Netball 1, while Army won Women's Netball 2 by 48-40.

Army also made a clean sweep in basketball, with the men's team beating Police 35-15, while the women's team thrashed Police 30-1.

Army ended Police's eight-year winning streak in football after securing a 1-0 victory to reclaim the Sukuna Bowl football title.

Police won the Mixed Touch Rugby competition after edging Army 4-3.

Meanwhile, Police are aiming for their fifth consecutive Ratu Sukuna Bowl rugby title when they face Army tomorrow at 4pm at the HFC Bank Stadium.

Police have won the rugby title for four consecutive years, from 2022 to 2025.

item.title: RFMF ends eight-year Sukuna Bowl football title drought with 1-0 win over Police
item.description: The Republic of Fiji Military Forces has ended an eight-year wait to reclaim the Sukuna Bowl football title after defeating the Fiji Police Force 1-0. RFMF secured the victory through an early goal by Gabriel Matanisiga, who found the back of the net to give the military side a 1-0 lead at halftime.
item.content:encoded:
The Republic of Fiji Military Forces has ended an eight-year wait to reclaim the Sukuna Bowl football title after defeating the Fiji Police Force 1-0.

RFMF secured the victory through an early goal by Gabriel Matanisiga, who found the back of the net to give the military side a 1-0 lead at halftime.

The team maintained its advantage throughout the match to seal the win against its long-standing rivals.

RFMF Head Coach Savaira Ratu says the victory was the result of careful preparation, discipline and the players' commitment to the team's strategies.

Ratu says selecting the final team was challenging, with 35 players initially in camp before the squad was narrowed down to the best 18.

She says the players prepared both mentally and physically, while the coaching team also worked on several tactics ahead of the match.

Reflecting on her halftime message, Ratu says she drew inspiration from the Bible, reminding the players that they were representing the RFMF and had a responsibility to give their best regardless of the outcome.

She says the players were reminded that winning or losing was not just about them individually, but about representing the entire military force.

Ratu also thanked God for giving the team the strength to get through the full 90 minutes.

The victory ends RFMF's eight-year wait for the Sukuna Bowl football title, adding another chapter to the long-standing sporting rivalry between the military and police forces.

The annual Sukuna Bowl competition brings the two forces together through various sporting contests, promoting teamwork, discipline and sporting spirit.

item.description: The Army women's team has made history in the 2026 Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl Basketball Tournament, defeating Police 30–1 in their first appearance, while the Army men's team beat Police 34–15.
